summary: The Epstein Files Transparency Act (Public Law 119-38) requires the Attorney General to publish all unclassified records, documents, communications, and investigative materials held by the Department of Justice regarding the investigation and prosecution of Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell. The documents must be made publicly available in a searchable and downloadable format within 30 days of the act's enactment. It prohibits withholding documents based on embarrassment or political sensitivity, though it permits specific exceptions for victim privacy, active federal investigations, classified national security information, child sexual abuse materials, and images of death or injury. Additionally, the Department of Justice must submit a report to Congress within 15 days of the release detailing the categories of information released and withheld, summaries of any redactions, and a list of all government officials and politically exposed individuals named in the files.

affected_groups.effect: Must review, compile, declassify to the maximum extent possible, and publish a large volume of investigative records within 30 days, as well as submit a subsequent report and Federal Register justifications for redactions.
affected_groups.group: Department of Justice and Attorney General

affected_groups.effect: Any such individuals named or referenced in the published materials or DOJ reports will have their names disclosed without redactions based on political sensitivity or reputational harm.
affected_groups.group: Government officials and politically exposed individuals

affected_groups.effect: Their personally identifiable information and personal or medical files are protected from disclosure to prevent an unwarranted invasion of privacy.

key_provisions: The Attorney General must make all unclassified Department of Justice records regarding Jeffrey Epstein, Ghislaine Maxwell, flight logs, and related entities publicly available in a searchable and downloadable format within 30 days.
Prohibits withholding, delaying, or redacting records on the basis of embarrassment, reputational harm, or political sensitivity.

Permits the withholding or redaction of specific materials, including victims' personal information, child sexual abuse materials, active investigation details, images of death or injury, and classified national security information.

Requires any redactions to include a written justification published in the Federal Register and submitted to Congress, and mandates the declassification of classified information to the maximum extent possible.

Requires the Attorney General to report to Congress within 15 days after the release, providing a summary of categories released, a summary of redactions, and a list of all government officials and politically exposed persons named in the materials.
missing_information: The total number of documents or pages to be released is not specified.
The exact cost or resources required by the Department of Justice to fulfill the mandate are not stated.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Epstein Files Transparency Act (Public Law 119-38) requires the Attorney General to publish all unclassified records, documents, communications, and investigative materials held by the Department of Justice regarding the investigation and prosecution of Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell. The documents must be made publicly available in a searchable and downloadable format within 30 days of the act's enactment. It prohibits withholding documents based on embarrassment or political sensitivity, though it permits specific exceptions for victim privacy, active federal investigations, classified national security information, child sexual abuse materials, and images of death or injury. Additionally, the Department of Justice must submit a report to Congress within 15 days of the release detailing the categories of information released and withheld, summaries of any redactions, and a list of all government officials and politically exposed individuals named in the files.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation mandates the public release of a wide array of federal investigative files regarding a high-profile criminal case within a strict 30-day timeline. Because the law restricts the use of reputational or political sensitivity as grounds for withholding documents and specifically requires the reporting of named government officials, it alters how the Department of Justice handles transparency and Congressional oversight for this specific body of records.
